title: Reconcile embedding/rerank/function-call charges for partial successes & throttled requests
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Summary:
There are multiple customer reports and internal audits showing discrepancies between tokens/embedding units billed and the expected usage for non-chat endpoints (embeddings, rerank, and structured function-calling outputs). These discrepancies occur in two main scenarios: (A) requests partially completed by the runtime due to internal throttling, quota enforcement, or upstream timeouts, and (B) requests that trigger tool calls/structured outputs where the function invocation itself consumes additional compute but is not consistently attributed to the originating API call for billing or quota enforcement.

Background / Why this matters:
- Customers are seeing over- or under-charges that do not match logs and Datadog dashboards; finance and support tickets have increased.
- Current meter pipeline assumes request->response is atomic; partial responses or mid-request fallbacks (e.g., model swap or truncated KV cache events) break that assumption.
- Rate limiter and quota enforcement currently operate on request arrival and rely on best-effort cancellation downstream; in-flight resource usage is sometimes not rolled back or attributed correctly.
- For embedding/rerank endpoints we also have cases where re-tries, batching, and partial failures cause duplicate meter events or missing attribution to the original client API key.

Scope (in):
- Instrumentation and accounting for embeddings, rerank, and function-calling on non-chat endpoints (structured outputs) across hosted + dedicated.
- Fix meter emission logic so that: (1) partial/failed responses emit a reconciled usage record that reflects actual tokens/embedding steps that executed, and (2) function-invocation compute is attributed to the parent API call.
- Update rate limiter interaction so quota tokens reserved for a request are reconciled on cancellation/failure and not double-counted.

Scope (out):
- Chat endpoint rework (separate project).
- Long-term billing model redesign (we will maintain current per-token/embedding unit model).

Problem details and examples:
- Example A: Customer requests embeddings batch of 100 inputs. At T+30s, runtime throttles due to GPU contention and returns embeddings for first 60 inputs; remaining 40 are cancelled. Billing shows full 100 embedding units charged. Logs show worker executed only 60 encodes.
- Example B: Rerank request triggers an internal function call to an external re-ranker plugin. Plugin execution consumed tokens and GPU time, but the emitted meter event used a generic worker id and lost the original API key mapping.
- Example C: Structured response with multiple function calls where the second call is retried by the runtime after a transient failure; two meter events are created with identical attribution, resulting in duplicated charge.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Ground-truth metering at the worker process: require that every embedding/rerank/function call execution emits a micro-usage event (micro-meter) with the minimal fields: request_id, api_key_id, model_variant, op_type (embedding|rerank|func-call), units_consumed (int), timestamp, and finality_flag (partial|final|compensated). These events are immutable and append-only.
2) Reconciliation service: build a small consumer that aggregates micro-meter events per request_id and emits a reconciled invoiceable event only when a request reaches a final state or when a reconciliation timeout elapses. The reconciled event contains summed units and an attribution key.
3) Rate limiter handshake: when a request is accepted, reserve quota tokens in the rate limiter with a reservation_id. On cancellation or failure, the worker must emit a compensation micro-meter referencing reservation_id so the reconciliation service can decrement reserved tokens and avoid double charge.
4) Function-call attribution: require the function runtime to forward parent request_id and api_key to every plugin invocation (or wrap invocation with a short-lived signed context). The plugin must include those fields in any micro-meter it emits.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- We will accept eventual consistency for billing (reconciled events may be emitted up to a few minutes later) in exchange for correctness and simpler worker-side instrumentation. This preserves low-latency response while centralizing final charge computation.
- Micro-meter events add noise to our Kafka stream and storage; we will keep the schema minimal and TTL micro-meter raw logs after 7 days. Reconciled invoiceable events are persisted for 90 days per finance needs.
- We avoid modifying API response payloads for customers; charging corrections are applied in billing records and support dashboards only.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 1 (3 days): Worker-side change to emit micro-meter events in embeddings and rerank code paths and include reservation_id for rate-limited requests. Add lightweight schema in kafka topic billing.micro_meter_v1. Tests: unit + integration local.
- Phase 2 (4 days): Reconciliation service prototype (consumer + aggregator) that reads micro-meter events and emits reconciled usage to billing.events topic. Implement timeout-based finality and compensate on cancellation. Deploy to staging.
- Phase 3 (2 days): Function runtime changes to propagate parent request_id and api_key through plugin invocations. Update plugin SDK. Backwards compatibility: if plugin doesn't send parent_id, reconciler attempts best-effort attribution using worker metadata; emits a warning label.
- Phase 4 (2 days): Rate limiter integration: reservation handshake, cancellation flow, and tests.
- Phase 5 (2 days): QA, rollout plan, and dashboards: add reconciliation metrics, Foglight/Datadog dashboards for mismatches, and a support tool to surface adjusted charges.

Acceptance criteria:
- All partial/failed embedding/rerank requests in staging result in reconciled billing records that match worker logs (within ±0 units).
- Function-call compute appears under the parent API key in reconciled events for >99% of test invocations.
- No duplicated charges observed in a 48-hour synthetic load test that injects transient failures and retries.
- Support dashboard surfaces reconciliation differences and allows searching by request_id.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Canary deploy micro-meter emission to 10% of traffic in staging for 48 hours, followed by 25% production canary for 24 hours. Monitor reconciliation latency and mismatch rate.
- If mismatch rate > 0.5% or reconciliation errors spike, rollback micro-meter feature and investigate.

Monitoring and SLOs:
- Metric: reconciliation.latency.p50/p95, mismatch.rate (reconciled_units != worker_logged_units), missing-attribution.rate (function-call events without parent_id). Target mismatch.rate <0.1%.
- Alerting: page on mismatch.rate >0.5% sustained for 10m or reconciliation consumer lag > 5m.

Follow-ups / future work:
- Expand same model to chat endpoints (separate ticket).
- Consider deduplication keys for retried function calls to avoid duplicate plugin-meter emissions at source.
- Finance-facing billing export update to include reconciliation metadata (original and reconciled usage).

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Reconcile+micro-meter+for+embeddings
- Prototype consumer branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/compare/feature/reconcile-micro-meter
- Support dashboard mock: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X-example-support-dashboard
- Datadog board: https://app.datadoghq.com/dash/abc123/reconciliation-overview

Risks:
- Plugin authors may not adopt context propagation immediately; we mitigate with best-effort attribution but will show warnings for manual support action.
- Increased Kafka throughput and storage costs for micro-meter events (budget approved but monitor actual ingestion).
